workItems.title: Close critical remote-administration and runtime security paths
workItems.rationale: Dedicated-server chat can reach RCON dispatch without validating the configured password, making the current path unsafe for remote deployment.
implementationScope: Disable chat-triggered RCON immediately
Create a separate authenticated admin channel
Validate tokens/secrets in constant time
Add roles, least privilege, expiry, replay protection, rate limits, and audit logs
Separate local console and remotely invocable command registries
Document the threat model and security owner
acceptanceCriteria: Anonymous and normal clients cannot invoke any administrative command
Invalid, expired, replayed, downgraded, or rate-limited credentials fail closed
Every attempt is auditable without logging reusable secrets
Remote administration is disabled by default
performanceBudgets: Admin authentication does not block the simulation thread
websiteImpact: The site must label remote administration unsafe/unavailable until this item closes
risks: Retaining a compatibility backdoor to the old chat command
outOfScope: Building a full hosted operator dashboard
definitionOfDone: Threat model and audit format are reviewed

workItems.title: Establish software supply-chain and dependency policy
workItems.rationale: Workflow actions use mutable major tags, dependency inventories disagree, CodeQL builds only part of the product, and releases lack SBOM/provenance/security gates.
implementationScope: Pin actions to commit SHAs
Make dependencies.lock authoritative and generate other inventories
Add vulnerability, license, secret, and artifact malware gates
Expand CodeQL across all shipped products and website scripts
Define severity exceptions with owner and expiry
Feed SBOM/provenance into release
acceptanceCriteria: No unpinned action or unmanaged dependency remains
Critical/high findings block without an owned expiring exception
Final package inventory reconciles with source lock
Release artifacts include verifiable supply-chain evidence
performanceBudgets: Security scans complete inside merge/release SLAs
websiteImpact: Security and supply-chain language links to exact passing evidence
risks: Scanner noise leading to blanket exclusions

workItems.title: Fuzz and bound every stable-v1 untrusted file and package parser
workItems.rationale: Saves, scenes, assets, shaders, archives, manifests, and crash metadata cross stable-v1 trust boundaries without a unified fuzz/bounds gate; packet and script campaigns belong to the excluded networking and scripting surfaces. 2026-09-05 progress (partial hardening, no fuzz harness): Json::ParseBounded/JsonLimits budgets on every default parse entry point; mod.json and mod config capped at 64 KB / depth 16 / 4096 nodes and parsed strictly; scene manifests capped at 8 MB / 100,000 entries with path containment; .spk decompression ratio bounded at Open; .skel/.sanim name-length and parentIndex validation; Spark::IsVirtualPathSafe. Tests/TestSecurityParsersReal.cpp now executes the shipped parsers (the packet-validator evidence is tracked under NET-100). Do not promote a JSON-fuzz claim: only bounded regressions were added.
implementationScope: Create libFuzzer/AFL-compatible targets and seed corpora for save, scene, asset, shader, archive, manifest, and crash inputs
Set file, allocation, depth, and time limits
Run ASan/UBSan fuzz smoke on every change and longer scheduled campaigns
Persist minimized regressions as tests
acceptanceCriteria: Malformed input cannot cause crash, OOB, path escape, integer overflow, or unbounded allocation/time
Every found issue lands with a minimized regression fixture
Required fuzz smoke is deterministic and blocking
websiteImpact: Parser/protocol safety claims require current fuzz evidence
risks: Fuzz harnesses bypassing production entry points
outOfScope: AngelScript and visual-script fuzzing behind G11
definitionOfDone: Budgets and regression workflow are enforced
Remaining: Tests/Fuzz harnesses over the production parsers, fuzz-smoke CI lane, minimized regression fixtures

workItems.title: Replace placeholder transport security with audited authenticated encryption
workItems.rationale: MMOFPS authentication fields can carry plaintext credentials, while engine networking includes XOR/MT19937/FNV placeholder security that cannot support a secure-networking claim. 2026-09-05 progress (no promotion): PacketValidator string screening is now enforced through schema-declared stringFieldOffset/NO_STRING_FIELDS (the sanitizeStrings flag was removed), ChatMessage is one NetBuffer string at offset 0, UTF-8 text is accepted, and the packet.stats string counter is a real count; Tests/TestPacketValidator.cpp and Tests/TestPacketValidatorReal.cpp execute the shipped validator. The transport still carries the XOR/MT19937/FNV placeholder security, so no secure-networking claim changes.
implementationScope: Adopt maintained DTLS/TLS or reviewed AEAD handshake/library
Use CSPRNG keys/nonces and authenticated sessions
Add replay windows, key rotation, downgrade protection, packet bounds, and protocol negotiation
Remove or isolate placeholder crypto
Redact credentials from logs/crash data
Obtain independent security review
Fuzz packet framing, negotiation, replay windows, and malformed encrypted traffic through the production transport
acceptanceCriteria: Packet capture contains no reusable credential or plaintext authentication data
Tamper, replay, nonce reuse, wrong key, truncation, reorder, downgrade, and malformed handshake fail closed
Authentication and gameplay share the production encrypted path
No custom cryptographic primitive remains in the advertised transport
commands: rg -n "mt19937|FNV|XOR|placeholder for DTLS|placeholder for AES|char pass" SparkEngine/Source GameModules/SparkGameMMOFPS
performanceBudgets: Encryption overhead fits the declared server tick and bandwidth budgets
websiteImpact: Do not use secure/encrypted networking wording until this item and review evidence pass

workItems.title: Define and implement the production online-service boundary
workItems.rationale: Engine networking and reference modules do not provide turnkey identity, matchmaking, fleet, secrets, abuse, moderation, entitlement, billing, or incident control-plane services.
implementationScope: Define engine SDK contracts versus product-owned services
Specify identity/session/match/fleet/admin/presence/moderation/entitlement interfaces
Create local deterministic adapters and production integration points
Add secrets/configuration management and dependency failure semantics
Prove versioned client/server/service compatibility
acceptanceCriteria: A deployment diagram and API contract name every trust/ownership boundary
Engine runs locally with deterministic adapters
Production adapters fail safely and are observable
No local JSON/demo service is marketed as production infrastructure
performanceBudgets: Service dependencies have explicit timeout/retry/circuit-breaker budgets
websiteImpact: Service claims distinguish engine interfaces, local adapters, and external product infrastructure
risks: Expanding engine scope into a hosted SaaS product
outOfScope: Operating a public production service during engine release
definitionOfDone: Failure modes and support policy are documented

workItems.title: Make multiplayer persistence transactional, migratable, backed up, and recoverable
workItems.rationale: MMO/MMOFPS reference persistence is local/demo-grade and does not prove atomic ownership, schema migration, concurrent writes, backups, restore, or disaster recovery. 2026-09-05 progress: AsyncDatabase's key-value store no longer truncates the live file on every write, so the interrupted-write acceptance now also covers that store (Tests/TestSaveSystemRoundTripReal.cpp, AsyncDatabaseReal_*); MMO/MMOFPS module persistence is unchanged and the item stays open.
implementationScope: Define transactional repository interfaces and idempotency keys
Version schemas and migrations
Enforce ownership and optimistic/concurrency controls
Encrypt sensitive data and separate secrets
Implement backup, point-in-time restore, corruption handling, and audit history
Provide deterministic local test adapter
acceptanceCriteria: Concurrent character/economy/territory writes cannot duplicate or lose state
N-1 migrations and rollback fixtures pass
Forced process/database failure recovers to a documented point
Backup restore is regularly rehearsed
performanceBudgets: Persistence latency and queue depth fit the declared server tick/SLO budgets
websiteImpact: Local persistence is never framed as production-ready until this evidence exists
risks: Binding the engine to a single database vendor

workItems.title: Secure and complete crash reporting, telemetry delivery, and symbol operations
workItems.rationale: Crash manifests can write GitHub/SMTP credentials to plaintext temporary files, trust unsafe screenshot paths, and claim upload behavior that is not implemented; telemetry drops failures without durable retry.
implementationScope: Remove reusable credentials from manifests/client configuration
Use controlled relay and scoped ephemeral authorization
Restrict crash directories and canonicalize/allowlist all file paths
Add redaction, consent, retention, size, and deletion policy
Implement truthful queued/delivered/rejected/failed states
Publish private symbols indexed by build ID and verify symbolication
Add durable telemetry spool/retry/drop accounting
acceptanceCriteria: Crash artifacts contain no reusable secret
Malicious manifest/symlink/path input cannot read or delete outside owned crash data
Declined consent transmits nothing
A synthetic release crash reaches the test relay and symbolicates to source
Endpoint outage recovers within documented spool/drop bounds
performanceBudgets: Crash handling is bounded and avoids deadlock/allocation in compromised process context
Telemetry queue has explicit byte/event limits
websiteImpact: Crash upload and telemetry wording stays local/incomplete until canary evidence passes
definitionOfDone: Privacy/retention policy and runbook are reviewed

workItems.title: Add production server observability, load, soak, backup, and incident gates
workItems.rationale: Profiling utilities and local chaos scripts do not substitute for externally consumable health/readiness, SLOs, alerts, long soaks, backup/restore, and incident response evidence.
implementationScope: Expose structured logs, metrics, health, readiness, and build/version identity
Define frame/tick/network/persistence/error SLOs and alerts
Run multi-process loss/latency/load/chaos/soak scenarios
Automate backup, restore, failover, rollback, and incident drills
Publish capacity and degradation envelopes
Own production network administration, telemetry, backup/restore, and incident rehearsal excluded from stable-v1
acceptanceCriteria: Operators can detect, diagnose, drain, restart, and recover a failing server
Thirty-minute release smoke and longer scheduled soak show bounded memory/queues and pass p95/p99 budgets
Backup/restore and alert/runbook drills are recorded
Telemetry is externally consumable and exact-SHA labeled
websiteImpact: Scale and reliability wording names the tested envelope instead of broad production claims
risks: Synthetic loads not matching real gameplay
outOfScope: Guaranteeing capacity outside the tested envelope

workItems.title: Make performance, memory, startup, package size, and visual regression release gates
workItems.rationale: Profiler and benchmark scaffolding exists, but no representative regression budget, committed golden-image baseline, blocking long soak, or previous-release comparison protects users.
implementationScope: Create representative Windows D3D11 client, SparkEditor, SparkGameFPS, and Windows NullRHI scenes
Set frame, headless tick, startup, memory, and package-size budgets for the supported row
Commit reviewed D3D11 golden baselines with GPU/driver metadata
Run long Windows NullRHI leak/deadlock soaks
Compare against the previous accepted stable-v1 release
Require reviewed approvals for budget and baseline changes
acceptanceCriteria: Budgets block regressions
Golden changes require reviewed baseline update
Required soak completes without leak, crash, deadlock, or unbounded queue growth
Results attach to exact commit and certified hardware row
performanceBudgets: The versioned budgets produced by this work item are themselves the acceptance surface
websiteImpact: Performance claims show scene, platform, hardware, percentile, and commit
risks: Noisy shared runners; use controlled hardware for promotion
outOfScope: Production service load, fleet capacity, backup, and incident budgets owned by OPS-110 and G12
